findings.where: First screen, the hero photograph (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The direction is 'Mark at work': a full-bleed photograph of Mark speaking, with his line over the calm side. Here the backdrop is cut away, so a head and shoulders float on flat slate, much larger than life. Nothing shows he is speaking. The lectern and the event are gone, and only the edge of a microphone is left at the bottom. The hero now reads as a portrait on a dark ground, which is v6's lever on v4's ground, not a picture of him at work. At this size, a cut-out face next to a statement line looks like a campaign poster.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for a new direction (v7) distinct from the portrait and dark-ground tiles, and for 'refined, never slick or salesy'. Staff at a development bank, who should see an adviser in action at a real event. A giant cut-out face reads closer to a politician's poster than to counsel.

findings.where: First screen, the header lockup 'Mark M. Moseley | MMM Infra mark' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The name comes first in position but not in weight. It is set small and light, while the white arches and 'MMM INFRA' beside it are larger and brighter, so at a squint the firm's mark wins over the man's name.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose personal-advisor test asks that his name leads with the logo beside it. When the mark outweighs the name, it reads as 'the firm is the brand', which brand sheet §5 rejects.

findings.where: First screen, around the action 'Write to me directly' (and the page as a whole)
findings.fault: Nothing on the first screen, or anywhere on the homepage part, shows evidence of standing. There is no region or place of his work, no body that asked for his advice, no legal background, and no recent talk with its venue next to the action. The one dated piece of work, the 23 April 2026 lecture, sits at the very end of the article specimen, with no venue.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank and agency staff who hire against terms of reference. They need to see that he has done this kind of work, for bodies like theirs, in their region, before writing (first-visit trust items 2, 3, 6 and 'Feel the CV'). Without that, the address is a cold ask.

findings.where: First screen, the caption 'Placeholder: Mark's photo from the current site, until the image round' (desktop)
findings.fault: The caption sits at the bottom left, under the text column and the blue action, about 400 px from the photograph on the right. By proximity it groups with the words and the action, not with the photo it labels.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging the first screen first, who needs to know at a glance which element is the stand-in. A caption under the action reads as small print about the email, not as a note on the photograph.

findings.where: Phone first screen, nav row 'Profile · Articles and talks · Blog' above the photograph
findings.fault: The top of Mark's head runs right up under the nav row, with no space between them. The nav looks as if it sits on his head, and the header and the photo merge into one cramped group instead of reading as two.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor opening the site from a LinkedIn link. The first screen looks crowded and unplanned just where the brief asks for calm and refinement.
